characterization_methods.key_findings: 12Al-20Mn-1C in the hot-rolled condition has a macro-hardness of 357 HV (Table 5).
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 5 kg load; 5 indentations per sample; applied to all alloys in all processing conditions (hot-rolling and tempering)
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure macro-hardness of the hot-rolled (as-received) reference condition and compare with heat-treated states

characterization_methods.key_findings: Optical microscopy was performed on all alloys at the hot-rolling and tempering conditions; no specific optical description is reported for the hot-rolled 12Al-20Mn-1C.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Through-thickness embedding, grinding and polishing performed separately for hot-rolled and heat-treated samples
characterization_methods.purpose: Analyse the microstructure of all alloys at different processing conditions, including the hot-rolled condition

computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Temperature range 0-1300 °C; composition 12Al-20Mn-1C; phases considered include BCC_A2, FCC_A1, KAPPA_E21, LIQUID, BCC_2SL
computational_details.simulation_method: CALPHAD equilibrium phase-fraction calculation (amount of all phases vs temperature)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Used qualitatively to explain austenite thermodynamic stability gradients between hot-rolling (1150 °C) and tempering; the text notes hot-rolled conditions at 1150 °C differ from the equilibrium assumption

processing_steps.method: vacuum induction melting and casting into ingots
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Alloyed steels produced by casting using a 100 kW vacuum induction furnace, resulting in 0.5 kg ingots (composition within Table 1 ranges: Al 9-12, Mn 10-20-30, C 0.4-1, Fe bal.).
Ingots were hot-rolled at 1150 °C obtaining 5 mm flat-products.
Hot-rolling was followed by water quenching, yielding the hot-rolled (as-received) reference state.

measurement_conditions.test_standard: Vickers macro-hardness, 5 kg load, 5 indentations per sample

unmapped_findings: The hot-rolled condition (1150 °C + water quenching) is the shared 'as-received' reference state used for comparison in all the study's hardness tables (Tables 2, 4, 5, 8, 9).

For 12Al-20Mn-1C, only the hot-rolled hardness (357 HV) is reported; microstructural/EDS characterization in the paper (Figs. 5-8, Tables 6, 7) pertains to the tempered conditions (600 °C / 800 °C) of this alloy, not to the hot-rolled state.
The 12Al-20Mn-1C composition falls within the tested Fe-Mn-Al-C ranges of Table 1 (Al 9-12, Mn 10-20-30, C 0.4-1 wt%, Fe bal.).

In the 12% Al alloy group the thermodynamic gradient for austenite stability between hot-rolling and tempering is reported as reversed relative to the 9% Al alloys (Fig. 12(c)), i.e. austenite is less stable at 800 °C than at 1150 °C for 12Al-20Mn-1C.
